text:
maria: Heads-up — cluster-autoscaler kicked on gpu-pool-3 and started scale-down ~6m ago. A few model-serving pods are stuck in Terminating because their PDBs prevented eviction :eyes:. Anybody seen CA/GPUs interact like this recently? /cc @oncall-sre

oncall-sre: digging in now. CA logs show it chose node-7 as unneeded and attempted drain. kube-controller-manager reported PDB violations: model-serving-prod-* (PDB minAvailable: 2 of 3). CA waited, then the cloud provider terminated the VM after 30s. Result: pods in Terminating and kubelet couldn't finish cleanup.

alex: CA will not forcibly delete pods that would violate a PDB — it should leave the node if it can't evict. If the cloud provider kills the VM first we get stuck pods. So two failure modes: PDB too strict, or VM termination too fast after drain initiated.

priya: We added PDBs to protect canaries during rolling updates, but maybe they're too rigid for scale-down. PDB supports minAvailable or maxUnavailable. For model-serving we could switch to `maxUnavailable: 1` so a scale-down can succeed without violating availability intent.

kevin: Another angle: many of these pods don't have a priorityClass set. If we give critical long-running inference pods a higher priority, CA won't evict them (and will pick different nodes to delete). Conversely, low-priority batch jobs should be evictable.

maria: Short-term mitigations: 1) set gpu-pool-3 min size = current to stop further scale-downs 2) increase cloud instance termination grace window if possible 3) temporarily relax PDBs for affected deployments. Long-term: safer drain flow for GPU nodes (cordon -> mark -> wait for graceful eviction -> terminate VM). I propose a tiny controller/operator to orchestrate that.

oncall-sre: temp fix applied: min size bumped. Also added alert to avoid auto-scale-down during active deployments.

alex: Implementation notes: cluster-autoscaler has flags `--scale-down-delay-after-add` and `--scale-down-unneeded-time`. Increasing those buys time. CA respects PDB but will try to evict; if eviction blocked it should not delete node group membership unless cloud API races. We should ensure CA waits for drain completion before calling provider delete. Might be a config mismatch.

priya: Proposed plan (for PR):
1) Update model-serving PDBs to `maxUnavailable: 1` where possible (safe for most services).
2) Create PriorityClass `gpu-protected` (value: 200000) and apply to pods that must not be evicted during scale-downs.
3) Build operator: on CA scale-down of GPU node, operator will annotate node `redwood.io/eviction-in-progress=true`, extend `deletionGracePeriodSeconds` for pods on that node and coordinate graceful drain with cloud termination API (delay termination until kubelet reports pods gone).
4) Tune CA flags: `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m`, `--scale-down-delay-after-add=15m` for gpu pools.

kevin: Runbook notes for oncall (if it happens again):
- Prevent further scale-down: `gcloud container clusters resize ... --node-pool=gpu-pool-3 --num-nodes=<current>` or equivalent for AWS
- Patch PDB to relax: `kubectl patch pdb model-serving-prod -p '{"spec":{"maxUnavailable":1}}'`
- Manually cordon & drain (if safe):
```
kubectl cordon node-7
kubectl drain node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300
```
Note: `kubectl drain` will fail if PDB blocks. You either patch PDB or scale deployment down slightly.

maria: Quick PR opened to change PDBs and add the PriorityClass. I’ll prototype the operator this week. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/pulls/482 (CI green) :+1:

eng-sre-bot: deploy-status: PR #482 opened by maria to update PDBs and add gpu-protected PriorityClass. CI passed.

priya: Adding this to eng-sre backlog as `triage/gpu-drain-safety`. Tentative rollout: tomorrow 21:00 UTC. Maria to own operator prototype, Alex will review CA flag changes, Kevin handles runbook updates.

maria: thanks all — I'll post updates in this thread as I push PRs and the operator prototype. If anyone sees repeat terminations, ping me directly. :fire:
